
---
title: "Task 5 – Visualising Your Universe"
format: html
---

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

my_data <- read.csv("solar_system_planets.csv")
```

# 5.1 Base R Histogram

```{r}
hist(my_data$mass,
     main = "Distribution of Planet Mass",
     xlab = "Mass (kg, relative units)",
     col = "lightblue",
     border = "white")
```

# 5.2 ggplot2 Scatter Plot

```{r}
ggplot(my_data, aes(x = radius, y = gravity)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth() +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Radius and Gravity",
    x = "Radius (km)",
    y = "Gravity (m/s^2)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 5.3 ggplot2 Boxplot

```{r}
ggplot(my_data, aes(x = type, y = distance_from_sun, fill = type)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Distance from Sun by Planet Type",
    x = "Planet Type",
    y = "Distance from Sun (10^6 km)"
  ) +
  theme_light() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

# 5.4 Faceted Plot

```{r}
ggplot(my_data, aes(x = gravity)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10, fill = "coral", color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ type) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Gravity Across Planet Types",
    x = "Gravity (m/s^2)",
    y = "Count"
  )
```

# 5.5 Saving the Plot

```{r}
p <- ggplot(my_data, aes(x = radius, y = gravity)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth() +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Radius and Gravity",
    x = "Radius (km)",
    y = "Gravity (m/s^2)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("my_universe_plot.png", p, width = 8, height = 6)
```
